title: Report a committed Supervisor change when a later VKS update is rejected
prompt:
Complete `VcfVksCoordinatedChange/VcfVksCoordinatedChange.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module for one coordinated vSphere Supervisor namespace and VKS Cluster change.

Before implementing, research the VCF 9.1 vSphere Automation API operations `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_getV2` and `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_update` and their generated VMware VCF PowerCLI 9.1 bindings in official VMware sources. Also research GET and JSON merge PATCH behavior for the namespaced `Cluster` resource in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` using official Kubernetes project sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer. The Kubernetes resource requests are not VMware operationIds; do not represent them as such.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. Keep the manifest prerequisite on the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` module version `13.5.0.25380678`; it loads the real `VMware.Bindings.vSphere.Api.IVcenterNamespacesInstancesApi` binding and model types. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, bindings, or specifications. Use the supplied genuine binding for vCenter and `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` for Kubernetes. Do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, or raw sockets.

Preserve and export only this function:

`Invoke-VcfVksCoordinatedChange -NamespaceApi <IVcenterNamespacesInstancesApi> -KubernetesBaseUri <string> -KubernetesToken <string> -Supervisor <string> -Namespace <string> -ClusterName <string> -ClusterClass <string> -NamespaceDescription <string> -TargetVersion <string> [-SkipCertificateCheck]`

Validate every scalar input before traffic. Names, class, description, version, and token must be nonblank. Reject CR or LF in the bearer token. `KubernetesBaseUri` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with root path and no credentials, query, or fragment. The client must not follow redirects.

The workflow is ordered and has two preflights followed by two changes:

1. Call the genuine binding method `VcenterNamespacesInstancesGetV2($Namespace)` exactly once. Require a non-null response whose Supervisor is an ordinal, case-sensitive match and whose config status is `RUNNING`.
2. Send a bodyless Kubernetes GET for the exact named `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` Cluster. Require matching namespace, name, topology class, and a nonblank topology version.
3. Construct a genuine `VcenterNamespacesInstancesUpdateSpec`, set only its `Description`, and call `VcenterNamespacesInstancesUpdate($Namespace, $spec)` exactly once. A successful update returns HTTP 204 and is a committed change.
4. Send one Kubernetes JSON merge PATCH for the Cluster's target topology version. If this later change is rejected with HTTP 422, report that failure while preserving the committed namespace result.

A Kubernetes operational non-success must not erase knowledge of an earlier committed change. When the namespace update succeeds and the cluster PATCH returns HTTP 422, return one object with exactly `OverallStatus`, `NamespaceChange`, and `ClusterChange`. `OverallStatus` is `Failed`. `NamespaceChange` has exactly `OperationId`, `Namespace`, `Status`, and `Changed`, with operationId `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_update`, status `Succeeded`, and changed true. `ClusterChange` has exactly `OperationKey`, `Namespace`, `Name`, `Status`, `Changed`, and `HttpStatus`, with operation key `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2:namespaced-clusters:patch`, status `Failed`, changed false, and integer status 422. Do not throw for that HTTP 422. Do not include credentials, response bodies, or underlying transport exception text in output or errors.

Wire shape is exact. Percent-encode every dynamic path value as one UTF-8 RFC 3986 segment. Send `Accept: application/json` on all four requests. The genuine binding must send exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` header only to vCenter; send exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <KubernetesToken>` header only to Kubernetes. GETs have no body, Content-Type, or query. The vCenter PATCH has media type `application/json` (the installed generated binding emits the exact header `application/json; charset=utf-8`) and a body containing exactly `description`. Leave `resource_spec`, `access_list`, `storage_specs`, `vm_service_spec`, `content_libraries`, `network_spec`, `zones`, `edges`, and `infrastructure_policies` unset so the generated binding omits them rather than serializing null, an empty string, array, or object. The Kubernetes PATCH has exact `Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json` and body `{"spec":{"topology":{"version":"<TargetVersion>"}}}`. Omit `dryRun`, `fieldManager`, `fieldValidation`, `force`, and `pretty` entirely; never append a bare `?`.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. Edit only `VcfVksCoordinatedChange/VcfVksCoordinatedChange.psm1`; do not modify `tests/`, `docs/`, or `VcfVksCoordinatedChange/VcfVksCoordinatedChange.psd1`.
scenario: the Supervisor namespace description update commits with HTTP 204, then the VKS Cluster topology version merge patch is rejected with HTTP 422 and the returned ledger must preserve that partial-success boundary
constraint: the contract-derived loopback request log proves exact generated-binding and Kubernetes wire shapes, total omission of unset options, authentication separation, and exactly one attempt per named operation
